summary: Well-designed preregistered paired controlled-fault study that targets a clear NetOps gap (verifier-guided LLM repair on vendor-CLI templates). Execution and primary paired analysis are plausibly sound and reproducible given the archived artifacts; the reported paired counts, exact test, and bootstrap CIs are consistent. However the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic was not produced by the archived confirmatory summary and must be reconstructed or its unavailability justified; the manuscript's References appear to use identifier-only entries rather than a conventional IEEE bibliography and must be converted; and the exact preregistered harmful-change mapping (needed to reproduce the omitted confirmatory safety statistic) is not located or documented in the manuscript. Addressing these items is necessary before finalisation.
critical_issues: Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic (planned in the preregistration) was not computed by the archived confirmatory analysis; the manuscript acknowledges the omission but does not present the preregistered confirmatory result or a reconstruction from archived artifacts.

References in the supplied manuscript evidence appear to be identifier-only (DOI/arXiv/OpenAlex identifiers) rather than a conventional IEEE-formatted bibliography entry list; this violates the track/reference requirements and prevents standard citation verification in the paper body.

The preregistered harmful-change mapping (the exact rule/lookup mapping from per-episode validator violation codes to the preregistered harmful-overrepair indicator) is not included or pointed to by a precise archive path in the manuscript; without that mapping an independent reader cannot reconstruct the preregistered safety statistic from the archived raw traces.
required_revisions: Compute and report the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair paired statistic (counts, absolute difference guarded−baseline, 95% CI, and the preregistered test) by re‑running the archived summary step against execution/raw_results.jsonl using the preregistered harmful-change mapping; include results in Methods/Results and update the Disclosure/Limitations to reflect the outcome. This change must be resolvable from the archived artifacts and does not require new model calls.

Embed the exact preregistered harmful-change mapping in the manuscript (compact table or algorithmic description) or provide an explicit archive path (file path and artifact SHA-256) to the archived mapping used to label per-episode harmful edits so external auditors can reproduce the safety aggregation.

Replace identifier-only bibliographic entries with a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/arXiv as secondary metadata) and ensure every numbered in-text citation supports the proximate claim. Provide the finalized BibTeX/IEEE reference list in the manuscript and archive.
optional_revisions: Add a brief (one-paragraph) exploratory table summarizing per-fault-class discordant counts (labelled exploratory) to help interpret where diagnostics most helped; artifacts to compute this are archived.

Report the model-call cost / latency secondary estimand (model_call_cost_per_avoided_failure) from the archived execution accounting as an exploratory metric (machine-cost and wall-clock per successful repair) to aid operational discussion.

Provide a compact evidence-to-claim table or nearest-work comparison matrix as an archived supplement (or a one-paragraph summary) linking each main literature claim to the verified source used; this will strengthen the Related Work / positioning while preserving page budget.
